methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in AI & Software, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Callosum is an early-stage AI & Software company founded by Danyal Akarca and Jascha Achterberg. The broader AI & Software sector contains 12 known peers, comprising 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private firms including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. However, the company's stage remains undisclosed, as does its current valuation and total capital raised, which constrains peer-based analysis.

The peer-median method was deemed inapplicable to this valuation. Of the 12 same-sector comparables identified, none satisfied the narrow filtering criteria required for robust triangulation—specifically, no peers matched on stage, adjacent-stage positioning, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. The analysis would require a minimum of three datapoints within these constraints to produce a defensible median multiple; zero were available. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the heterogeneity of AI & Software company maturity and business model.

Without sufficient stage-matched or tier-matched peers, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range. The key uncertainty is stage definition: until Callosum's funding round stage (seed, Series A/B/C, or later-stage) is disclosed, peer selection remains infeasible. Public market data from Palantir alone lacks sufficient granularity to bridge this gap. A credible valuation would require either narrower peer identification once stage is clarified, or alternative methods such as DCF or revenue-multiple analysis using company-specific financial data, none of which are available here.
